edits.before: This file is the single normative source for how any Agent, on any Host, uses Clued. The Clued service serves it at `/clued-agent.md`; the `clued` Skill, repository `AGENTS.md` files and the MCP server instructions point here instead of restating it. Host- or repository-specific procedures may add steps; they never relax this contract. A working Binding or scope is required for every protected call but is never, by itself, a reason to read or write.
edits.after: This file is the single normative source for how any Agent, on any Host, uses BeamingFace. The BeamingFace service serves it at `/clued-agent.md`; the `clued` Skill, repository `AGENTS.md` files and the MCP server instructions point here instead of restating it. Host- or repository-specific procedures may add steps; they never relax this contract. A working Binding or scope is required for every protected call but is never, by itself, a reason to read or write.

edits.before: 6. Current-state answers come only from Clued. Any question about the current or latest state of the user's projects, records or of Clued itself — what is the latest or current version, what is frozen, fixed, accepted or cancelled, the current task, the latest decision, what changed — is answered only from records read in this session after `clued_session_resume` (§2.1). The Host's own memory, Host-side conversation summaries, earlier replies, cached files, repository snapshots and old checkpoints are not sources for such an answer, even when they appear to contain it; use them at most to decide what to search. Answering from them without the read above is a contract violation. When Clued cannot be read (no Binding, denied scope, unavailable service), say that the current state is unknown and why, instead of answering from those sources; for a denied scope, also request it (§6.7).
edits.after: 6. Current-state answers come only from BeamingFace. Any question about the current or latest state of the user's projects, records or of BeamingFace itself — what is the latest or current version, what is frozen, fixed, accepted or cancelled, the current task, the latest decision, what changed — is answered only from records read in this session after `clued_session_resume` (§2.1). The Host's own memory, Host-side conversation summaries, earlier replies, cached files, repository snapshots and old checkpoints are not sources for such an answer, even when they appear to contain it; use them at most to decide what to search. Answering from them without the read above is a contract violation. When BeamingFace cannot be read (no Binding, denied scope, unavailable service), say that the current state is unknown and why, instead of answering from those sources; for a denied scope, also request it (§6.7).

edits.before: When a material outcome happens in work you are doing for the user, write it to Clued in the same turn, before you report it as done. Do not wait for "remember this", for the end of the session, or for a reminder.
edits.after: When a material outcome happens in work you are doing for the user, write it to BeamingFace in the same turn, before you report it as done. Do not wait for "remember this", for the end of the session, or for a reminder.

edits.before: 5. In the reply, name what you wrote in one line (record ID and Receipt). If a write fails, say that it failed and why; never describe the outcome as recorded, and never call a local file or Markdown note a saved Clued record.
edits.after: 5. In the reply, name what you wrote in one line (record ID and Receipt). If a write fails, say that it failed and why; never describe the outcome as recorded, and never call a local file or Markdown note a saved BeamingFace record.

edits.before: 6. Write each outcome as it happens, before the next production action. When one turn merges a pull request, applies a migration and then starts a release, record the merge after the merge and the migration after the migration, and start the release last; do not batch the writes behind the release. Starting a deployment or release is not itself a §3 outcome: record it when its run has finished, from the run's result. Do not make a Clued call the next action after you start a deployment, release or other production action: Host-side permission checks judge a call by what happened just before it, and a Clued call made in that position has been refused as a production action although it changes nothing in production (§4.7). Verify a release through the release's own checks, not through an immediate Clued read.
edits.after: 6. Write each outcome as it happens, before the next production action. When one turn merges a pull request, applies a migration and then starts a release, record the merge after the merge and the migration after the migration, and start the release last; do not batch the writes behind the release. Starting a deployment or release is not itself a §3 outcome: record it when its run has finished, from the run's result. Do not make a BeamingFace call the next action after you start a deployment, release or other production action: Host-side permission checks judge a call by what happened just before it, and a BeamingFace call made in that position has been refused as a production action although it changes nothing in production (§4.7). Verify a release through the release's own checks, not through an immediate BeamingFace read.

edits.before: 7. Say what you are about to record before you write it, in one line of your reply: what (the record and its main claim), where (the scope) and on what authority (the Owner's words in this turn, or this section's rule that the Owner's tracked work is recorded without a reminder). Host approval layers judge a write from the visible conversation and the request; they do not see this contract or the Owner's rules stored in Clued, and a write whose authority was not visible has been refused as unauthorized persistent storage (§4.7). The line is a statement, not a question: §3 writes need no further confirmation from the Owner, and `user_confirmed: true` records where the claim came from, not a confirmation step.

edits.before: 6. Some Hosts show every HTTP 403 as "blocked by a firewall or security service". Clued returns 403 for authorization denials and for contract-rule rejections it has not yet mapped to a tool error, so check your arguments against the tool's contract before calling it a network or infrastructure failure, and label any unverified cause as a guess.

edits.before: 7. A Host may refuse a Clued call itself, before it leaves the Host: a permission classifier, a tool allowlist or a sandbox rule. The refusal comes from the Host, names the Host's reason (for example "denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier"), and the call never reached Clued. It is not a Clued error, a Binding, scope or currentness failure, or evidence that Clued is unavailable. Do not retry it unchanged, do not reach the same effect through another tool, another Binding or a different call, and do not write the outcome anywhere else as a substitute (§3.5 and §6.1). Say which call the Host refused and the Host's stated reason, say which §3 writes or §5 checkpoint are still owed because of it, continue the work that does not depend on them, and ask the Owner to allow the call. Once the Owner allows it, make the owed writes first (same idempotency keys), then continue.
edits.after: 7. A Host may refuse a BeamingFace call itself, before it leaves the Host: a permission classifier, a tool allowlist or a sandbox rule. The refusal comes from the Host, names the Host's reason (for example "denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier"), and the call never reached BeamingFace. It is not a BeamingFace error, a Binding, scope or currentness failure, or evidence that BeamingFace is unavailable. Do not retry it unchanged, do not reach the same effect through another tool, another Binding or a different call, and do not write the outcome anywhere else as a substitute (§3.5 and §6.1). Say which call the Host refused and the Host's stated reason, say which §3 writes or §5 checkpoint are still owed because of it, continue the work that does not depend on them, and ask the Owner to allow the call. Once the Owner allows it, make the owed writes first (same idempotency keys), then continue.

edits.before: 2. Before any `create`, `write`, `move`, `rename`, `replace` or `delete` that can affect a governed workspace, the Agent must use the registered deterministic preflight for that workspace and obtain the exact admission/capability required by the Host. The preflight binds the operation, source, destination, artifact role, relevant version/currentness identity, registered profile version, complete mutation request digest, trusted artifact-authority version and policy version. If the Host has no usable preflight path, mutation is unavailable: stay read-only and report the missing capability instead of bypassing Clued with a generic file tool. The registered workspace profile and artifact classification are Host-owned trusted configuration captured or resolved before mutation handling: `managed_root`, profile identity/version, allowed layout, registered external roots, governance class, artifact identity, deletion authority, Currentness identity and workspace version must not be accepted from the Agent's mutation payload as authority. Operation schemas are exact: `delete` has one source target and forbids a destination; `move`/`rename` require source and destination; `create`/`write`/`replace` require a destination and forbid a source. A Host-internal admission proof must be short-lived, single-use, unforgeable within that Host instance and re-verified against the exact mutation and current artifact-authority/currentness versions immediately before the side effect; it is not a bearer capability and must not be serialized or exposed for cross-process replay.

edits.before: 7. Official Host/Adapter implementations must route governed workspace side effects through the shared guarded mutation wrapper or an equivalent wrapper that proves the same ordering: Host-captured trusted registered profile → Host-owned artifact/currentness resolver → deterministic preflight → exact short-lived admission consumption → side effect. The transport-visible mutation surface must consume admission internally; it must not expose raw preflight, admission or commit tools. The mutation entry must reject a missing, forged, expired, already-consumed, cross-Host or binding-mismatched admission before the side effect; a direct generic file effect is not an equivalent implementation. Host qualification must fail when an open-world process tool is exposed, or when a generic filesystem mutation tool can reach the governed root, its parent/sibling boundary or another registered scan root. It must include negative fixtures for: direct mutation without preflight, caller-declared profile/root/classification/deletion authority/currentness, operation-shape confusion, status folders, Resource Center parent/sibling/root drops, other scanned unregistered Clued islands, deletion based only on duplicate bytes, and status inference from filenames. It must include a positive track→topic case and prove that a denied preflight invokes the side-effect function zero times. The official filesystem Adapter obtains watcher entries from its captured scan-root configuration and real directory enumeration rather than from the mutation caller. The deterministic parent/sibling watcher reports `UNAUTHORIZED_WORKSPACE_MUTATION` and normal scans never call a model; a model is invoked only for an exceptional ambiguity that policy explicitly permits escalating.

edits.before: 8. This contract does not claim that Clued can physically stop an unrelated third-party tool that already holds raw OS write permission. Until a Host uses a brokered writer, ACL or equivalent restricted write principal, such a channel is outside hard enforcement and must not be described as protected. Detection may report `UNAUTHORIZED_WORKSPACE_MUTATION`; physical non-bypassability requires the storage/Host boundary to remove generic write authority.

edits.before: 10. Storage reads and uploads are metered per rolling hour, per authorized client and per account; only the Owner sets these budgets, on the Clued storage page. On `budget_exhausted`, stop that kind of storage call, tell the Owner what is left undone and continue other work; do not retry in a loop, split the work across other Bindings or clients, or treat the Owner's budget as something the Agent may change.

edits.before: 11. Find a storage connection yourself; never ask the Owner for a `connection_id`. Every `clued_storage_*` tool takes the `connection_id` of one Owner-authorized storage connection, an internal ID the Owner should not need to know. Get it from `clued_storage_connections`: it lists the connections this client may use, each with its root folder's `name` and `managed_root`, its `project_id`, its `tracks`, the `write_levels` and `read` classes the Owner granted, and `normal_use`. Use the connection whose `name` or `managed_root` matches the storage the Owner named; when several match, ask the Owner to choose by name, never by ID. When the list is empty, or the connection lacks the level or read class the work needs, tell the Owner which storage and which level to turn on on the Clued storage page, and continue other work. When your Host does not list `clued_storage_connections` (a connection made before the tool existed), find the `connection_id` in Clued records with `clued_search_context` first; if none is found, tell the Owner to reconnect the Clued connector in this client so the tool appears, and still do not ask for the ID. The list is a hint, not an admission: each storage call checks its own grant when it runs. The same holds for every other internal ID a Clued tool can look up (a Drive file ID, a job, claim or record ID): look it up, never ask the Owner for it.

edits.before: - While you wait, do nothing for the merge: do not bring the default branch in again or push for it, and do not tell the Owner. Renew about once an hour to keep your lease (2 hours) without spending the claim's 12 renewals, each with a new `progress_ref` such as `merge-queue:<UTC time>`, and read `merge_queue`; a renewal keeps your place. When you become head, bring the default branch in and push if it moved, wait for CI and merge, or enable auto-merge once the Owner has turned on "Allow auto-merge". Where the clued-admission App may write, the `clued-merge-executor` workflow brings the default branch into an admitted, non-`protected` head that fell behind, and merges an opted-in head once its CI workflows passed, their gated jobs run. Non-`protected` PRs also opt in when claim renewal `progress_ref` equals the full current head SHA (case-insensitive); `protected` PRs still need the body line `Clued-Auto-Merge: <head sha>`. After admission it reruns a successful gate-only run once, within the title's rerun limit. Opt in when you join, after merge approval; another head needs new opt-in unless only merging the default branch into the body-approved head. Keep the claim live until the merge, and record it in Clued. Turn auto-merge off as soon as a CI required check fails or the merge is refused, and leave the queue then or when you stop: renew without the ref or release the claim. Never stay in it while you wait on anything else.

edits.before: - The Owner may run a Task as a race (multi-copy mode, turned on only by the Owner on the Clued page): several Agents work on it at once and the first result delivered is kept. A claim of such a Task returns `claim_mode` with your `copy_index`, the number of `copies` and the `shared_resources`. The other copies' claims of the same Task never conflict with yours, so do not stop for them. Work in your own place, your own branch and pull request and, in Clued storage, drafts outside the shared resources (for example under `_copies/<copy_index>/`); write to the shared resources only to deliver. The first copy that writes to them, or whose pull request merges, is adopted; the others are out. A copy that is out is refused with `copy_not_adopted` (a renew with `work_claim_not_active`) and its pull request fails admission: stop work on it, it has already ended. When every copy is taken, a claim is refused with `work_claim_copies_full`. Only the Owner turns a race on; never ask for one to get around a conflict.
